newsitem.title: UK: BANKERS QUESTION ASQUITH DMG JOB CHANGE.
newsitem.headline: BANKERS QUESTION ASQUITH DMG JOB CHANGE.

text.p: Bankers were on Wednesday puzzled by a top management change at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell (DMG), the investment banking arm of Germany's mighty Deutsche Bank AG.

The Daily Telegraph reported that Jonathan Asquith would relinquish his role as chief operating officer of the investment bank and would focus instead on DMG's UK operation. DMG declined comment on the report.
DMG insiders said the change had not been announced internally and the first they had heard of it was the Daily Telegraph report. The decision has still to be ratified by Deutsche Bank's board.
Some banking sources said the move was a logical one as Asquith had finished the job he was assigned to do of integrating the organisation and its controls with Deutsche Bank group.
Asquith, 40, was only given the post in January. He was previously chief financial officer and global head of equities. He joined the Morgan Grenfell, which was later taken over by Deutsche, in 1979.
But others said the move contradicted DMG's policy of establishing the business on product rather than geographical lines, questioning why the investment bank would change tactic.
"The real power lies with the heads of the product lines, most of whom are in London. This just creates a double reporting line," said one banker.
The Telegraph said Michael Dobson, DMG's chief executive, had taken on the role of chairman of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell Group, with Asquith chief executive of the London subsidiary.
Bankers said this move was recent and had followed the retirement in May of Sir John Craven as chairman of DMG. Craven has joined the advisory board of the Deutsche Bank group.
Dobson had become chairman of the UK subsidiary when Craven left and Asquith had moved into the chief executive's role, they said.
